🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Taddei Got Her Start Before Morena Even Existed</u>

The opposition wants to hang Guadalupe Taddei on Morena. Sheinbaum went through the record: Taddei took over Sonora's electoral institute in 2014, "when Morena didn't even exist yet," under PAN governor Guillermo Padrés, and the appointment was approved by the INE General Council headed by Lorenzo Córdova.

She reached the INE presidency in 2023 by tómbola, a random draw, because the Chamber of Deputies never reached a two-thirds majority. "If she committed crimes, let it be investigated," Sheinbaum said, and she wants a deep audit of the institute.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Business Council: 23 Stalled Projects Unblocked, $3.9 Billion Moving</u>

Mexico's top business council, the CCE, says domestic investment is finally flowing. Since the leaders of its 14 member associations met President Sheinbaum in early May, 23 stalled projects worth 3.9 billion dollars have been unblocked, CCE president José Medina Mora said.

After 0.5% growth last year, the council now expects 2% this year and 2.5% in 2027. The two bottlenecks it wants fixed are energy supply and water.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US Ambassador: The Terrorist Label Is Not About Bombing Mexico</u>

Ronald Johnson, Washington's ambassador to Mexico, told the Milken Institute's Global Investors Symposium that designating cartels as terrorist organizations does not mean the US wants to "drop bombs on Mexico." He said the label is about financial and legal tools: sanctions and anti-terror-financing measures aimed at traffickers, money launderers and shell companies.

Mexico's position hasn't moved: cooperation, yes. Foreign troops or strikes on Mexican soil, no.

🇲🇽🇮🇳 <u>Mexico and India Open Trade Talks</u>

Mexico and India formally opened negotiations for a Preferential Trade Agreement on October 28, signing the terms of reference that set its scope and roadmap. A Mexican business mission to India is planned for early 2027.

The numbers show why. In 2025 Mexico sold India $1.97 billion and bought $9.13 billion, a $7.16 billion deficit. Mexican exports to India fell 28% from 2024.

Priority sectors are autos, chemicals, electronics, pharma, agrifood, energy, critical minerals and medical devices. The talks follow up on the deal Sheinbaum and Modi struck at the G7 in June 2025. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🌉 <u>Amado Nervo Bridge Opens Between Jalisco and Nayarit</u>

Sheinbaum opened the Amado Nervo Bridge over the Ameca River on October 28. It links Puerto Vallarta with Bahía de Banderas and cuts travel times by up to 40 minutes.

It cost 963 million pesos and runs more than 800 meters, with three lanes each way and a bike lane. It gives an alternative to Federal Highway 200, which carries about 73,000 vehicles a day. Some 479,000 people benefit.

The bridge is named for a Nayarit poet and was paid for with public money.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>Mexico Will Have a New INE President by December 7</u>

The Chamber of Deputies will vote on November 4 on the call to replace Guadalupe Taddei at the head of the INE. Jucopo chief Ricardo Monreal says the process could wrap up "around December 6 or 7."

A five-member Technical Evaluation Committee, two named by the CNDH and three by the Jucopo, will review résumés, give exams and interview every applicant before the floor vote.

Exams, interviews and a public calendar. The INE's last presidents were never chosen this way.

🇲🇽🇺🇸 <u>Sheinbaum on the T-MEC: "Patience and Serenity"</u>

Trump says a trade deal is "close," then says it isn't. Sheinbaum's read: he's campaigning, with the US midterms on November 3. Her advice was "patience and serenity."

On substance, she says Mexico has resolved nearly every non-tariff barrier Washington flagged "without ceding sovereignty." Ebrard spoke with Commerce Secretary Lutnick about whether a deal is possible before the vote.

What is still missing is the one thing Mexico wants most: a real cut to the Section 232 tariffs on cars, steel and aluminum. Whatever the result on the 3rd, she said, the work doesn't stop.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Senate Moves to Strip the INE Presidency of Its Super Powers</u>

After Guadalupe Taddei's resignation amid the Cajas Graf and Zeg contract scandals, senators from Morena (Javier Corral, Susana Harp), MC (Amalia García), the PAN and the PRI all filed bills to amend Article 45 of the electoral law.

The target: the 2024 rule that lets the INE's president appoint executive directors and technical unit heads alone, without the General Council. The bills would hand those appointments back to the full council.

One person signing off on the people who run the elections was the problem. Morena's own senators are the ones moving to fix it.
banner: INE: SENATE MOVES TO CUT CHIEF'S POWERS

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Dies at 92</u>

Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, the man the system robbed of the presidency in 1988, died on October 28 at 92. Sheinbaum mourned him as "a man of firm principles, who transformed the political life of our country," and said his "dignity and republican conviction" remain an essential reference for the nation.

In 1988 the computers "crashed" and Carlos Salinas walked into Los Pinos. Cárdenas answered with a peaceful movement, not a riot, and nearly four decades later the left he built governs Mexico.

His father nationalized the oil. He spent his life keeping that idea alive.

🇲🇽🍅 <u>Ebrard: Trump's Tomato Duty Backfired</u>

The 17% US antidumping duty on Mexican tomatoes cut Mexico's exports and pushed up prices for American consumers without helping Florida growers, Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard said, as reported by El Financiero. The Economy Ministry puts the cost to Mexican exporters at more than 350 million dollars a year, in a trade worth about 2 billion dollars. "Who grew? Florida? No. Canada grew with its greenhouses, Guatemala grew, and other countries grew."
banner: TOMATO DUTY: US PRICES UP, FLORIDA NO GAIN
